fpocket finds 97 pockets on AF-O60566-F1-model_v6; max druggability 0.169 overall, 0.111 within the pseudokinase domain; no pocket centered at N1002 or L1012 (only pockets 7 and 19 touch residue 1002, both low druggability)
The stop-gain transcript is NMD-targeted: 748 nt from PTC (CDS 2209) to the last exon junction (CDS 2957), six downstream junctions (2284..2957), exon 17/23, 698 nt past the 50-nt rule; context TGAA

openFDA label for hydroxychloroquine sulfate states safety and effectiveness ESTABLISHED in pediatric patients for malaria treatment and prophylaxis; the same label limits the film-coated tablets to children of at least 31 kg because they cannot be crushed or divided
No ingredient ranks in the top 100 of all three screen lanes simultaneously

Verdict updates: hydroxychloroquine class promoted (Tang 2011 aneuploidy-selective vulnerability + established pediatric malaria label, with the >=31 kg tablet restriction narrowing the pediatric leg); metformin demoted (weak subordinate Tang 2011 evidence); NMN is best biological but status-blocked (in-vivo BubR1 raise in wild-type mice, North 2014; lawful dietary supplement since FDA's 2025-09-29 reversal of the 2022 exclusion, still not an FDA-approved medication); amlexanox unchanged bench-only (exposure gap ~10x); fostamatinib rejected as screen-flag-only (background-level LINCS read on a validation-limited lane)
Ataluren EU authorization ended 2025-03-28 after efficacy unconfirmed; amlexanox exposure vs potency gap ~5 uM serum vs >=50 uM effective

claims.claim: openFDA enrichment: 1,151 of 1,811 drugs matched a US label; 962 labels carry a Pediatric Use section

The NAD+ precursor class is absent from the 1,811-drug screen because of mechanism-record coverage, not scoring: ChEMBL 37 holds zero mechanism records for niacin (CHEMBL573) and nicotinamide (CHEMBL1140), and acipimox (CHEMBL345714) has one record with a null target and action 'Unknown'

Niacin is an FDA prescription drug (NIACOR ANDA040378 immediate-release plus multiple extended-release ANDAs) whose labels state pediatric safety and effectiveness are not established (extended-release: 16 years and under); acipimox has no FDA label or application

The BUBR1 nucleotide site is annotated by mapping the 14 ADP contacts of the Drosophila crystal 6JKM onto human residues 774, 781, 793, 795, 840-843, 886, 887, 889, 910, 911; the mapping recovers human K795 (the kinase-dead K795R residue) and puts the fly HRD aspartate at human R886, with 4 of 13 contacts identical

Two independent pocket finders agree there is no pocket at the mutation: p2rank's top pocket on AF-O60566-F1 is the nucleotide site (score 8.86, probability 0.406, contains K795) and its nearest pocket to N1002 is 25.05 angstrom away, while fpocket caps druggability at 0.169 overall and 0.111 in the domain

The docking instrument fails its own pose-recovery control: redocking ADP into 6JKM puts the top-scored pose 6.03 angstrom from the crystal pose, best-of-9 3.37 angstrom, against a 2 angstrom success bar

Docking 2240 approved molecules against three BUBR1 pockets returns no standout and no discrimination: ADP reaches only the 83rd percentile of the library in its own site with 372 ordinary drugs outscoring it, the known chaperone migalastat sits in the bottom 6 percent everywhere while lumacaftor sits above the 99th percentile in all three boxes, and no graded case candidate ranks near the top in any box, so the screen supports only the boundary statement that no approved molecule is a credible stabilizer candidate
